prTitle: feat(cdc/consents): refactor consent data extraction with deep search functionality

analysis.summary: The refactor introduces several high-severity breaking changes to the API contract, including property renaming and data type mismatches that will break existing consumers.

bugs.title: Breaking API Change: Property Renaming
bugs.description: The response properties 'Name' in both the subscriptions and preferences arrays have been renamed to 'name' (lowercase).
bugs.risk: This is a breaking change for all API consumers. Any frontend or downstream service expecting the PascalCase 'Name' property will receive 'undefined', leading to broken UI labels or logic errors.
bugs.codeSnippet:
-            Name: key,
-            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)
...
+            name: key,
+            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)[0],

bugs.title: Functional Regression: isSubscribed Type Mismatch and Undefined Risk
bugs.description: The logic for 'isSubscribed' changed from a guaranteed string (concatenated result) to the raw first element of 'deepFind'. If the field is missing, it now returns 'undefined' instead of an empty string. If present, it likely returns a boolean instead of the expected string.
bugs.risk: Consumers expecting a string (e.g., comparing against 'true') will fail when receiving a boolean. Additionally, returning 'undefined' for missing fields may violate the expected API schema, causing crashes in strict consumers.
bugs.codeSnippet:
-            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)
-              .map((item) =>
-                Array.isArray(item) ? item.join(``) : item?.toString() || ``,
-              )
-              .join(``),
+            isSubscribed: deepFind(value, `isSubscribed`)[0],

bugs.title: Breaking Change: isConsentGranted Type Mismatch
bugs.description: Similar to isSubscribed, 'isConsentGranted' was previously forced to a string. The new 'findConsentItems' returns the raw value (likely a boolean) from the CDC object.
bugs.risk: Existing consumers expecting a string representation of the consent status will face type mismatch errors. The ConsentItem interface also incorrectly declares 'value' as a string while the logic assigns raw (likely boolean) objects to it.
bugs.codeSnippet:
preferences: accountData.preferences
-      ? Object.entries(accountData.preferences).map(
...
+      ? findConsentItems(accountData.preferences).map((item) => ({
+          name: item.key,
+          isConsentGranted: item.value,
+        }))

notBugs.reason: The shift from extracting names from 'customData' to using the JSON path is noted as a 'deep search' refactor in the PR title, suggesting this behavior change is an intentional feature of the new implementation.

While searching arrays with Object.entries results in numeric indices in the path (e.g., 'item.0'), this is technically correct behavior for a generic deep search and depends on whether the CDC data structure contains arrays in the preferences block.
